classification.difficultyReason: Fill improper and mixed labels on two number lines, one in fifths from 0 and one in quarters from 2. The student must read the start value as 8/4 and group wholes, as in p9-q4.

answer.worked: Each interval is one fifth, so count fifths from $0$. Below the line, group every five fifths into one whole and keep the leftover fifths. Thus $\frac55=1$ and $\frac{10}{5}=2$.

Each interval is one quarter. The left endpoint is $2=\frac84$, so count quarters from there. Below the line, group every four quarters into one whole and keep the leftover quarters. Thus $\frac{12}{4}=3$ and $\frac{16}{4}=4$.
